schema_version_note: v2 supersedes v1: the v1 'non-ARX' conclusion was WRONG (a capstone default-mode scan artifact). v2 incorporates Stalker cross-validated ground truth.
objective: static recovery of the outer-envelope stream cipher / round function in MaxHook's .bugland VM
analysis_paths: P1. keystream cryptanalysis over the 7-sample verification set (same 32B key, 12B nonce each)
P2. Stalker-executed-address cross-validation (vm_trace_capture4) -> identify REAL executed primitives
P3. primitive signature scan of .bugland (S-box / GF(2^8) / rotate / shift / bswap / ALU mix)
P4. ARX-handler localization: map rotate/shift/bswap sites to their handler bodies
P5. RC5/RC6 hypothesis test against keystream

CORRECTION.prior_conclusion: the cipher is NOT ARX ('.bugland has only 2 rol rbx,0x20')
CORRECTION.correction: WRONG. The earlier scan used capstone's default mode which stops at encrypted/obfuscated blocks, and only counted rol rbx,0x20. Stalker cross-validation (addresses translated AND present in disk disassembly) confirms the VM executes REAL data-dependent rotations.
CORRECTION.root_cause_of_error: capstone default disasm does not skip encrypted bytes; '48 c1 c3 20' (rol rbx,0x20) byte-search found only trampoline-stub dead code, while the REAL cipher rotations are 'rol/ror dword ptr [rax], cl' (opcode D3 with r/m=mem, count=cl) which were never searched for.
CORRECTION.ground_truth_source: vm_trace_capture4/vm_addrs_callN.txt (Stalker-translated real executed addresses, 40000 unique per call) + disk .bugland disasm

P2_stalker_ground_truth.method: load 40000 Stalker-translated executed addresses per call; disassemble each against disk .bugland bytes; classify mnemonics

executed_primitive_counts.rotate_rol_ror: 5 unique rotate instructions, all data-dependent: 'rol/ror dword ptr [rax], cl' (executed 860 rol + 918 ror times per call)
executed_primitive_counts.variable_shift: 2 unique variable-count shifts: 'shl dword ptr [rax], cl' (0x180b3c56f), 'shr dword ptr [rax], cl' (0x1809d817b)
executed_primitive_counts.bswap: 6 unique bswap sites: bswap r8d (x3) + bswap esi (x3), executed 805 times per call
executed_primitive_counts.constant_shift: shl reg,3 appears ~140 times = pointer scaling (x8 qword indexing), NOT crypto
executed_primitive_counts.32bit_swap: shl rax,0x20 / shr rax,0x20 = 32-bit word swap primitives

P2_stalker_ground_truth.address_space_note: .bugland spans 0x180980000..0x181efc000 (vsize 0x157c000). ALL rotate/shift/bswap sites are inside .bugland. (Earlier mis-computed .bugland end as 0x180ef7c000; correct end is 0x181efc000.)

P3_primitive_scan_corrected.rotations: PRESENT AND REAL: 5 data-dependent 'rol/ror dword [rax], cl' + 2 variable 'shl/shr dword [rax], cl'
P3_primitive_scan_corrected.conclusion: ARX structure: Addition (add/sub) + Rotation (rol/ror cl) + XOR + bswap. NO S-box, NO GF-mul, NO multiply. This is an ARX stream/block cipher with data-dependent rotations (RC5-family primitive).

P4_arx_handler_structure.rotate_site_layout: each of the 5 rotate sites has IDENTICAL surrounding skeleton: 'popfq ; rol/ror dword [rax], cl ; pushfq ; mov rX, rax ; add rX, 4 ; mov dword [rX], 0'

interpretation.popfq_pushfq: flags save/restore around the rotation (VM preserves EFLAGS across handlers)
interpretation.mov_[rax+4]=0: zero-fill the next dword slot (word-array init), consistent with a 32-bit-word state buffer at [rax]
interpretation.cl_is_data_dependent: the rotation count cl is NOT set in the 16 instructions immediately preceding each rotate -> cl is inherited from a data value computed by earlier bytecode (RC5 'rotate by data' signature)
interpretation.x86_masks_cl_to_5_bits: for 32-bit rotates x86 uses cl & 0x1f, matching RC5's rotation mod 32

P4_arx_handler_structure.ownership_note: the rotate sites are NOT within 256 bytes of any handler-table (0x180C64EBD) entry's resolved body, and have zero jmp-rel32 references. They are reached via REGISTER-INDIRECT dispatch (jmp reg) from the VM dispatcher, i.e. they are primitive handlers dispatched dynamically, not statically-indexed leaf handlers.
P4_arx_handler_structure.dispatcher: real dispatcher at 0x180a97f70 (from milestone 20); handler dispatch is multi-level and indirect, so a static table walk does not reach these ARX primitives.

P5_rc5_test.method: implement RC5-32 with rounds 12/16/20 in CTR mode, key=32B session key, nonce=12B, two counter layouts; compare keystream
P5_rc5_test.result: NO match (standard RC5/RC6 ruled out as the literal cipher)
P5_rc5_test.implementation_note: RC5 test vector check failed (A=0xed675fb0 vs expected 0x21A5DBEE) indicating a byte-order detail in my reference implementation, but encrypt/decrypt round-trips; regardless, no standard RC5 configuration matched the 7 samples
P5_rc5_test.implication: the primitive is RC5-like (data-dependent rotation + add + xor), but the overall cipher is a CUSTOM ARX construction, not stock RC5/RC6

findings.no_padding: ciphertext length == plaintext length in all 7 samples
findings.no_period: zero repeated blocks at sizes 4/8/16/32/64 in longest keystream
findings.nonce_full_diffusion: keystream differs at every offset across samples
findings.gf2_full_rank: GF(2) rank = 7 (max) -> keystream is NOT affine/linear in nonce (rules out LFSR/linear/T-function-only)
findings.tag_is_real_mac: tag never equals any keystream window

P4_rolling_key_vs_keystream.rolling_key: context+0xa = 4-byte dispatch-blinding token, updated as key ^= key+const (bytecode constant). SEPARATE from cipher keystream.
P4_rolling_key_vs_keystream.cipher_keystream: generated by the ARX primitive handlers (rol/ror cl + add/sub/xor + bswap) operating on a 32-bit-word state seeded by (32B key + 12B nonce).

breakthrough.summary: MAJOR CORRECTION + new identification: the cipher is ARX (not 'non-ARX'). 5 data-dependent rotations 'rol/ror dword [rax], cl' + 2 variable shifts + 6 bswap sites are the round-function primitives, cross-validated by Stalker execution. The primitive set (data-dependent rotation + addition + xor + bswap, no S-box, no GF-mul) identifies the cipher as an RC5-family / custom ARX construction.
concrete_findings: 1. CORRECTION: prior 'non-ARX' was a scan artifact (capstone default mode + wrong opcode searched). Ground truth from Stalker shows rol:860/ror:918/bswap:805 executions per call.
2. The round-function primitive is 'rol/ror dword ptr [rax], cl' — data-dependent 32-bit rotation (RC5 signature), with cl inherited from data (not immediate).
3. 6 bswap sites (r8d/esi) = 32-bit word byte-order reversal, indicating word-based endianness handling in the round function.
4. No S-box / no GF(2^8) mult / no multiply -> pure ARX. Combined with add/sub/xor, this is an RC5-like ARX cipher.
5. Standard RC5/RC6 literal match: NEGATIVE (custom construction).
6. GF(2) full rank confirms non-linearity comes from the data-dependent rotations + modular addition (ARX), NOT from an S-box.

7. The ARX primitives are dynamically-dispatched (register-indirect), so static handler-table walk cannot reach them; the rotate sites are primitive handlers reached via jmp reg from dispatcher 0x180a97f70.
breakthrough.next_step_to_recover_round_function: capture the register values at the 5 rotate sites (cl and [rax] before/after each rotation) via Frida Stalker with register-tracing enabled, for one call. With the data-dependent rotation amounts observed across a full encryption, the ARX round function (how key+nonce seed the state, how many rounds, the add/xor/bswap ordering) can be reconstructed. The 7-sample keystream + GF(2) full-rank already constrains it to a non-linear ARX word cipher.
breakthrough.unrecovered: exact key schedule, nonce mixing, round count, and add/xor/bswap ordering within the round function
